JUDGMENT FACTUAL BACKGROUND 1.

Succinctly stated, the case of the prosecution is that on the basis of a secret information that some persons were running an office in the name of Telco Industries Ltd and were duping gullible youths with Rs 1800 each in the name of providing jobs in Telco Industries, a raid was conducted on 17.06.2000 at E8 Chand Bagh Wazirabad Road, Delhi.
Upon such raid, three persons namely Ashwani Kumar, Hoshal and Parvez Khan were apprehended at the spot and one Vinod Joshi (Complainant) also came at the spot.

MODUS As per prosecution, the accused persons duped the gullible youth on the pretext of providing them jobs in the following manner:
.
An advertisement was published in local newspaper advertising that certain jobs are available and the application forms of which were available in the market and near court.

. The form was required to be sent to the address at Telco Industries Co. Ltd.
2115, Mukimpura, Old Subzi Mandi Road, New Delhi.

DECISION & REASONS 16.
I have bestowed my thoughtful consideration to the rival submissions made before me.
Evidence and documents on record have been perused carefully.

Accused persons are indicted for the offences U/s 420/465/468/471/469/34 IPC.
17.

The allegations of the prosecutions against the accused persons are three fold:
. 420 IPC:
As per prosecution, the accused persons cheated one Niranjan Nayak and Govind Chand Nayak of Rs 1800/ each on the pretext of providing job.

It is alleged that accused persons forged the appointment letters,
receipts and other material with the intent to cheat and also issued the said documents to candidates for appointment with the knowledge that the same are forged documents.
It is alleged that the accused persons forged the visiting card of JTC education centre and thereby harmed the reputation of complainant Vinod Joshi.

18. Regarding the allegations of cheating i.e. 415/420 IPC by accused persons with Niranjan Nayak and Govind Nayak of Rs 1800/ each in the name of providing job, it is noteworthy that Govind Nayak remained untraceable during the trial and could not be examined by the prosecution.
Niranjan Nayak was examined as PW8 and he did not support the prosecution on material aspects.
He stated that he had read about the vacancies in Telco Industries in an advertisement in a local newspaper and had also filled the form.
But this witness denied that he received back any form with visiting card or that he met accused Hoshal and gave Rs 1800/ to him.
He denied his signatures on the personal search memo of accused Hoshal and the seizure memo of receipt pads alleged to be recovered from accused Hoshal.
It is noteworthy that personal search memo of accused Hoshal i.e. Ex PW4/D bears the name of Niranjan Nayak and Govind Nayak.
PW Niranjan Nayak denied his signatures and Govind Nayak could not be examined by the prosecution as he remained untraceable.
In such circumstances, the recovery of Rs 3600/ and receipt pad from accused Hoshal becomes doubtful.
It is also pertinent to mention that neither the personal search memo nor the seizure memo bears the signature of FIR No.258/2000 State Vs. Ashwani Kumar & Ors.

Further it is the case of prosecution that advertisement was issued in the newspaper regarding vacancies i.e. inducement was done by way of advertisement.

In this regard, it is very essential to note that the IO of the case Insp H.S.Saini during his crossexamination stated that he does not know the language in which the advertisement Mark QA1 & QA2 were written and that he had not filed the translation of the same from any expert.

He further stated that he had not inquired as to who had got published the publications QA1 and QA2 i.e. the advertisements meaning thereby it can not be fastened upon the accused persons that they had got the advertisement published and thereby induced the candidates to apply and wrongfully hand over the registration charges to the accused persons.

Thus, it can be safely stated that prosecution could not prove beyond reasonable doubt that accused persons dishonestly induced Niranjan Nayak or Govind Chandra Nayak to deliver the registration fee of Rs 1800 each to accused persons.
19.

Regarding the allegations of forgery and consequential offences, it is pertinent to refer to the definition of 'forgery'
463.

Forgery--Whoever makes any false documents [or false electronic record] or part of a document [or electronic record,] with intent to cause damage or injury, to the public or to any person, or to support any claim or title, or to cause any person to part with property, or to enter into any express or implied contract, or with intent to commit fraud or that fraud may be committed

,
commits forgery.
20. It would also be necessary to understand the scope of Section 464 IPC in this context FIR No.258/2000 State Vs. Ashwani Kumar & Ors.

or Thirdly.--Who dishonestly or fraudulently causes any person to sign, seal, execute or alter a document or an electronic record or to affix his electronic signature on any electronic record knowing that such person by reason of unsoundness of mind or intoxication cannot, or that by reason of deception practised upon him, he does not know the contents of the document or electronic record or the nature of the alteration.
